subject: Dedicated capacity: oscillating-burst guardbands & autoscale SLO (Stellaar)
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@stellaar.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Jasper Cole <jasper.cole@stellaar.ai>, Stellaar SRE <ops@stellaar.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Initial: expected burst windows + contract implications

Lauren / Ben —

Thanks for the run-through last week. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we prep for next quarter's launch:

- We expect a 2.5x traffic spike during our nightly ingest window (00:00–03:00 PT) for the first 6 weeks post-launch.
- Peak concurrency is approximately 420 concurrent generation workers at 1.6k tokens/sec average.
- We want a predictable cost model and won’t tolerate >25% latency SLO misses for the production "high" tier.

Questions: Can Redwood guarantee a burst policy for Dedicated that lets us absorb that 2.5x without having to pre-reserve 3x baseline? What crediting or amortization options exist if we pre-agree a shoulder pool or ephemeral headroom?

Can you propose a concrete guardband approach (numbers + throttles + rollback) we can take to procurement?

Thanks —
Marta
Head of Platform, Stellaar Analytics

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@stellaar.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Jasper Cole <jasper.cole@stellaar.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: expected burst windows + contract implications

Hi Marta —

Appreciate the numbers. Short answer: yes — we can support an oscillating burst profile without forcing a 3x reserved slab, but we need to formalize the guardbands and the crediting model so both sides have predictable economics and SLAs.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll run a quick sizing model against your traffic distribution and propose a two-tier burst construct:
   - Shoulder pool: pre-committed slab (30–40% over baseline) for predictable daytime variance.
   - Ephemeral headroom: transient preemptible GPUs that scale to cover the 2.5x ingest windows (auto-evicted outside bursts).
2) Autoscale policy we suggest: continuous batching with a 60s smoothing window, aggressive prewarm at T-10m, and a canary scale to +25% before full ramp.
3) Credit model: bill baseline reserved usage at the committed rate; ephemeral headroom billed at on-demand rate but we introduce a monthly burst credit that refunds a portion of ephemeral spend up to an agreed cap.

I’ve looped in Ben for the sizing spreadsheet and Karhtik for the operational rollback/canary language. We’ll attach a capacity model and a draft amendment for procurement.

—Lauren
Director, Dedicated Sales
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@stellaar.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: expected burst windows + contract implications

Marta —

Attached is a quick sizing run (attachment: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)) that maps your nightly ingest to GPU-hour needs under three profiles: steady, shoulder-heavy, and burst-peaky. Key outputs:
- Baseline reserve (steady): 160 A100-equivalent GPUs.
- Shoulder pool (30%): +48 GPUs reserved as a slow-scaling buffer for daytime variability.
- Ephemeral headroom to reach 2.5x at peak: additional ~240 preemptible GPUs for a 3-hour window.

Operational notes:
- We recommend configuring the ephemeral headroom as preemptible G-reserve instances with a max reclaim latency of 30s and a staged eviction policy (least-recently-used batch jobs first).
- Canary flow: when telemetry shows 60% of baseline concurrent, trigger a canary to +25% for 10 minutes; if latency <20% above SLO, continue to ramp.

I also attached a draft amendment (draft-amendment-stellaar.pdf) with a burst credit table — suggestion: 15% monthly credit applied to ephemeral spend for the first 3 months, then review.

Let me know if you want the spreadsheet split by quantization profile (Q4_8 vs Q5_0) — that materially affects GPU-hour numbers.

Cheers,
Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jasper Cole <jasper.cole@stellaar.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@stellaar.ai>, Stellaar SRE <ops@stellaar.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 14:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: expected burst windows + contract implications

Thanks for the detail. A few clarifying points from SRE/procurement:

- Can you commit to a maximum preemption window and earliest-reclaim ordering? We run stateful KV cache use during ingest and need graceful eviction.
- How are billing meters reported for ephemeral headroom (per GPU-second or per token)? We need per-minute granularity for internal chargebacks.
- The 15% credit is a good start but procurement will ask for a ramp (15% → 10%) after month 3 unless we have telemetry proving lower ephemeral spend volatility.

Also: if we rely on preemptible headroom, what fallback exists if preemptible capacity is unavailable in-region? We need a cross-region fallback or local lower-capacity quantized-model fallback.

Appreciate the attachments — will review and send back markups by Wednesday.

—Jasper
Platform Engineering Lead, Stellaar

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jasper Cole <jasper.cole@stellaar.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@stellaar.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: expected burst windows + contract implications

Jasper —

Operational commitments we can formalize in the amendment:
1) Preemption window: max 30s reclaim signal; application-level drain hook with 45s grace before force reclaim.
2) Billing: ephemeral headroom metered per GPU-minute; we’ll surface that at the job / allocation-level in the console and provide a per-minute CSV export for your chargeback system.
3) Fallbacks: primary fallback is cross-region routing to our secondary US region (same SLA band) if local preemptible pool is exhausted; secondary fallback is auto-failover to a quantized model (Q4_8) pinned per-deal with slightly relaxed latency SLO.
4) Canary & rollback: formal policy — canary to +25% for 10m; full ramp to target over 8 minutes; auto-rollback if 3 consecutive latency windows (1m each) exceed 30% above target.

I’ve added a small runbook (warm-pool-runbook.md) to the Drive link for your SRE team describing the drain hook and eviction prioritization.

If those are acceptable, Ben and I will bake the exact phrasing into the amendment.

—Karthik
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@stellaar.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800

Lauren / Team —

This looks good and answers most questions. Two minor asks before procurement signs: a) include explicit numeric cap on refundable credits per month (we propose $25k) and b) add a clause for an emergency bilateral overflow (if both local and cross-region preemptible pools are constrained, Redwood will provide a temporary throttled on-premise-like reduced-latency corridor or a prioritized queue for 7 days while we work the capacity uplift).

If you can accept those addenda, we’ll get procurement moved and target an execution this month. I’ll upload markups to the Drive doc and ping your team when done.

Thanks —
Marta
